name: Pentlatch
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Andreatta, Mat, Jessie Recalma & Suzanne Urbanczyk. 2023. Boas and the Babblefish (Part I): Turning pentl'ach Vowels into Consonants. Papers for ICSNL 58 (Reisinger et al. eds.), pp. 1-9. Vancouver: UBCWPL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only transcriptional: p.7 'We have also found the accent mark used to indicate primary stress.' and p.7 '..the accent mark is to be interpreted as an indicator of stress, rather than a glottal stop.' Boas's <V'V> = V + syllable-final glottal stop. No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Andreatta, Mat, Jesse Recalma & Suzanne Urbanczyk. 2024. Boas and the Babblefish Part 2: Making Sense of pentl'ach c-cedilla symbols. Papers for ICSNL 59 (Reisinger et al. eds.), pp. 1-12. Vancouver: UBCWPL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; consonant (dental/alveolar fricative and affricate) correspondences only.

sources.citation: British Association for the Advancement of Science. 1890 [publ. 1891]. Sixth report on the north-western tribes of Canada (Boas's second general report on the Indians of British Columbia, incl. 'Comparative vocabulary of eighteen languages spoken in British Columbia', row 9 PEntlatc). CIHM 14338; archive.org scanned text.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Pentlatch appears only as accent-marked word forms in the comparative vocabulary (e.g. koi'yil); the grammatical notes cover Bilqula, Snanaimuq, Shuswap etc., not Pentlatch.

sources.citation: Qualicum First Nation. pentl'ach language / The pentl'ach alphabet (web page).
sources.note: Nothing; alphabet picture-word list in community orthography without stress marks.

sources.citation: Pulhug, Alena. 2023. Reconstructing pentl'ach plural and diminutive noun reduplication for language reclamation. Honours thesis, Dept. of Linguistics, University of Victoria.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Reconstructs reduplicated forms from Boas's accent-marked corpus; likely states where stress sits in plain vs. reduplicated stems (the closest thing to a stress generalization for pentl'ach).

sources.citation: Galloway, Brent D. 1988. Some Proto-Central Salish sound correspondences. In William Shipley (ed.), In Honor of Mary Haas, 293-343. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.

sources.note: Contains the published key to Boas's Pentlatch transcription (p. 302) and Pentlatch reflexes; may comment on stressed-vowel correspondences.

sources.citation: Kinkade, M. Dale. 1985. Pentlach reduplication. Paper presented at the Fifth Working Conference on Central Salish Languages, Victoria, BC. (and Kinkade n.d., pentl'ach vocabulary database with Salish cognates, University of Washington Special Collections 51008-005)
